# dbd — Database Designer

> A standalone CLI and embeddable Rust library for managing database schemas as code.

dbd parses SQL DDL files, resolves dependencies, generates migrations, loads data, and deploys to PostgreSQL, Supabase, SQLite, or Convex — all from a single binary with zero runtime dependencies.

## Core concept

SQL files are the source of truth. Path = `ddl/<type>/<schema>/<name>.<ext>` (roles have no schema): `<type>` ∈ table|view|materialized_view|function|procedure|enum|sequence|role, ext `.ddl`|`.sql`. Folder = type, parent = schema, filename = entity name. There is no `ddl/extension/` or `ddl/schema/`: extensions go in the target's `extensions:`, schemas under `schemas:` (`inspect` refuses such a file; `doctor` names the entry). Singular type folder is canonical (plural accepted but `dbd doctor --fix` migrates it to singular).
- `ddl/table/config/lookups.ddl` → entity `config.lookups` (table)
- `ddl/view/config/genders.ddl` → entity `config.genders` (view)
- `ddl/materialized_view/analytics/daily_sales.ddl` → entity `analytics.daily_sales` (materialized view; write `create materialized view if not exists …` + trailing `create [unique] index …`)
- `ddl/procedure/staging/import_lookups.ddl` → entity `staging.import_lookups` (procedure)

Files are parsed once into a rich internal representation (Entity + TableDef). That same structure drives every feature: dependency graph, apply, migrations, DBML generation, data import.

## design.yaml structure

```yaml
project:
  name: MyProject

source:
  dialect: postgresql
  search_path: [app]           # the path a file with no `SET search_path` runs on (apply/deploy/reconcile/combine prepend `SET search_path TO app, public`); a migration or hook stating none runs on it too (none set ⇒ `RESET search_path`)

target:                        # ONLY the first entry is read; the URL scheme picks the adapter
  postgres:                    # key `supabase` = same adapter + Supabase rules (see below)
    url: $DATABASE_URL         # -d / $DATABASE_URL override it
    extensions: [uuid-ossp]
    roles:
      - name: app_user
    skip_schemas: [auth]       # target owns these schemas — exclude their entities from the design
    grants:                    # {schema: {role: [perms]}} — any target key, applied by apply, deploy and reconcile
      config: { app_user: [usage, select] }

schemas:
  - config
  - staging:
      grants: { app_user: [usage, select] }   # merges with target.grants
      exposed: false           # served by PostgREST? drives inspect's RLS report

apply:                         # lifecycle hooks around the DDL phase
  after:                       # runs on `apply`, `deploy` AND `reconcile`, before the grants and policies/
    - script: sql/realtime.sql
      writes: [app.messages]   # declare tables dbd cannot derive by parsing

import:                        # data files are found by convention: import/[<env>/]<schema>/<table>.<csv|tsv|json|jsonl>
  staging: [staging]           # schemas an import may load (it truncates them); others refused. Omit = no restriction
  options: { truncate: true, null_value: '' }
  tables:                      # per-table overrides only — NOT an allowlist
    - staging.legacy: { null_value: '\N' }
  after: [import/loader.sql]   # runs on `dbd import` and `dbd deploy` — NOT on `dbd apply`

export:                        # empty ⇒ every table; listed ⇒ only these (tables, views or matviews)
  - config.lookups

materialized_views:            # refresh scheduling for ddl/materialized_view/ entities (pg_cron)
  options:                     # shared defaults for every matview
    refresh: "0 2 * * *"       # cron expression; omit ⇒ no scheduled refresh
    concurrently: true         # needs a unique index on the matview
  overrides:                   # per-matview overrides (by qualified name)
    analytics.top_products: { refresh: "*/30 * * * *" }

dbml:
  base:
    exclude: { schemas: [staging] }
  core:
    include: { schemas: [config] }
    output: core.dbml          # filename (default: <key>.dbml)
    auto_group_by_schema: true # emit `TableGroup <schema>` per schema
    groups:                    # or explicit groups (precedence over auto)
      - name: lookups
        tables: [config.lookups, config.lookup_values]

scopes:                        # named entity subsets — deploy one design to many DBs
  hub:
    includes: [config, app.users]   # schema | schema.entity | schema.* (wildcard)
    deps: report               # report (default, errors on gaps) | include (auto-closure)
    extensions: []             # optional per-scope allowlist; omit=all, []=none, [vector]=subset
  reporting:
    excludes: [staging.*]      # wildcard drops a schema's entities but keeps the schema
  everything: all              # bare `all` = the full set; `all`/`default` are reserved names

ignore: [bfs, my_company.*]    # exact names or prefix.* — matching references are not resolved

format: { keyword_case: lower, query_style: river }   # dbd format options
```

Parsed but not read (reserved): `import.options.format`, `import.tables[].env`, `target.schemas`, `target.path`, `external[].columns`. (`import.staging` is enforced from 0.25: a data file whose target schema it leaves out is refused, all of them named, before anything is truncated — on `import`, `import -f`, `deploy` and their dry runs.)

**The `supabase` target key** uses the same PostgreSQL adapter but (1) exposes `public` by default, (2) keeps Supabase's schemas (`auth`, `storage`, `realtime`, `graphql_public`, `supabase_functions`, `pgbouncer`, `pgsodium`, `vault`, `extensions`, `supabase_migrations`) out of `reconcile --prune`, (3) adds `GRANT USAGE` to `anon`/`authenticated`/`service_role` on every listed schema when any grants are configured, and (4) is the default protected set for `dbd reset` (which also protects `public`). `source.dialect: supabase` is just PostgreSQL for the reader.

Scopes are orthogonal to `target` (DB platform) and the connection: pair them at run time with `dbd deploy --scope hub --database $HUB_URL`. `includes`/`excludes` items are a bare schema (its entities + the schema entity), a qualified `schema.entity`, or a `schema.*` wildcard (same `prefix.*` syntax as `ignore:`; drops a schema's entities while keeping the schema — for `includes`, `schema.*` ≡ `schema`). A dependency gap (in-scope entity referencing a managed entity outside the scope) is an error under `report`; `external:` entities are never gaps. An optional per-scope `extensions:` allowlist restricts which `target.extensions` apply (omit ⇒ all, `[]` ⇒ none, `[vector]` ⇒ subset) — for deploying to a DB that lacks an extension; roles/externals stay always-on. Omit `default`/the block ⇒ full set; `--scope all` is always the full set. Sequences are selected like tables; a table depends on the enum its column is typed with, the sequence its default draws from and the function a trigger in its file runs (gaps reported, pulled in under `include`); a scope keeps the schema an allowed extension installs into, and one that excludes that schema by name while keeping the extension is refused by every command; grants follow the scope (a scoped apply/deploy grants only on the schemas it builds); a hook is skipped only when it touches a table the design manages outside the scope (an `external:` table or one the hook creates never causes a skip; its bare names judged as Postgres resolves them, along the path each statement runs on — its last `SET search_path`, else `source.search_path`, `public` after it — to the first schema where the design has that table or view), and an `apply.*` skip is named before the run and in the `apply`/`deploy`/`reconcile` dry runs (an `import.after` skip in `import`/`deploy --dry-run`); a scoped migration installs the roles and extensions it adds; a scoped `reset` never cascades (it refuses, dropping nothing, and names what outside the scope depends on what it would drop); roles and pg_cron refresh jobs are not narrowed. Every command that takes a scope except `graph` prints `scope 'X': N of M entities` (working set incl. the `include` closure, out of every entity, externals left out) — `diff --json` on stderr; `graph` puts the scope in its JSON. **A scope narrows what is applied, not what the project owns:** `reconcile --prune --scope` never drops a table the design declares outside the scope — upgrade to ≥0.24.1 before a scoped prune (earlier releases did, #40). **Scope guard:** the first `apply`/`deploy`/`reconcile` pins a database to its resolved scope (recorded in the bookkeeping table's `scope` column — `dbd.meta.scope` on Postgres/Supabase, `_dbd_meta.scope` on SQLite); a later `apply`/`deploy`/`reconcile`/`reset`/`import`/`export`/`refresh`/`policies` (and `reconcile --dry-run`, and the `apply`/`deploy`/`import`/`policies`/`reset` dry runs given a database) under a *different* scope is refused — an exact match: a DB pinned to `all` refuses `export --scope hub` — unless you pass `--allow-scope-change` on `apply`/`deploy`/`reconcile` (which re-pins the DB) — `reset --force` or `reset --allow-scope-change` bypasses it; `import`, `export`, `refresh` and `policies` have no bypass and never re-pin; `diff` and `migrate --status` write nothing, so they note the pin instead of refusing. After a `project.name` rename the pin (and every other mark) is read from the record the old name left, when the database holds the design's objects. Pre-existing DBs are unpinned until their next write.

## Commands

- `dbd init` — scaffold project (`--target postgres|supabase`; any other target is refused); or **reverse-engineer** a whole project + baseline snapshot from an existing source: `--from-db <conn>` (live DB; a database with both `auth` and `storage` schemas gets a `supabase` target, and only there are its platform schemas left out; every schema and extension left out is named; extensions go in the target's `extensions:`, schemas in `schemas:` — only those something was captured in, unless `--schema` named them — a table an FK reaches outside the project in `external:`; under `--schema` the extensions the captured objects use are declared (installed in `public` or a captured schema) and each other type/function/table they need from outside is printed as a `needs:` line; what the model cannot hold is a `warning:` line; re-runnable DDL, so the project applies back to its own DB and a fresh one with an empty `diff` — under `--schema`, to one that has what was named as needed) or `--from-dbml <file>` (DBML, mutually exclusive; `--target postgres|supabase`). Refuses against a dbd-managed DB (use `merge`) or an existing `design.yaml`. Flags: `--schema`/`--exclude-schema`/`--all-schemas`/`--roles`/`--version`/`--dry-run`; secrets stay out (`$DATABASE_URL`)
- `dbd merge` — sync a DB (or `--from-dbml <file>`) into the current project (reverse-engineer + reconcile; edits only `design.yaml`'s `project.version`, and warns about an undeclared extension, an external table the project neither declares nor builds, or an unlisted schema it wrote a file into, for you to add; a table declared `external:` is never captured — named `left out` — and an overwritten table file keeps its triggers — a SQLite table's too; `--from-dbml`, whose document holds none, keeps the triggers written in each file it rewrites, with their `SET search_path`): foreign or managed `D≥Y` → overwrite DDL + auto-snapshot the diff; managed `D<Y` → refuse (stale DB, no override); orphans reported never deleted; same selection flags as init
- `dbd inspect` — validate, report errors/warnings (+ scope dependency gaps with `--scope`, its advisory checks run over the scope, and a `deps: include` closure that needs what the scope excludes is refused); `--fix` auto-formats DDL files in place (`--fix --scope` only the scope's files); `-n` naming nothing is `no entity named 'X'`, and under a scope one it does not build `X is outside scope 'S'` (same on apply/graph/export/refresh), an `external:` one is refused, and `inspect -n` counts and advises on that entity alone; a `ddl/extension/` file, or a `ddl/schema/` one for a schema `schemas:` does not list, is an error (they belong in design.yaml — `dbd doctor` names the entry); a file that does not parse draws no `SET search_path` warning; under `--scope`, warnings in files the scope does not build are counted on their own line, not listed as the scope's; `--from-db` resolves references against the live catalog (uses `-d`/`--database`) and caches to `.dbd/refcache.json`. Surfaces unresolved migration `-- TODO:`s. **Exits 1 on blocking errors** (v0.12.0+; previously always 0), so it works as a CI gate — a parse error also states that `apply`/`reconcile`/`deploy` will refuse until fixed. Under `--scope`, errors are split into blocking vs `Out of scope — not blocking '<scope>'` by the same rule the run uses, so `inspect` and `apply` agree; out-of-scope errors don't affect the exit code but are never suppressed. Also prints an advisory `Suggestions:` section (Postgres/Supabase) for string-set `CHECK` constraints that could be enums — advisory only, never affects validity/exit code; proposals are grouped by value set, table-qualified on a name clash, and an identifier that is not a safe path segment is reported without a path
- `dbd apply` — apply schemas + entities + pending migrations (blocks while migration TODOs remain) in one dependency sort (type bands: schema, extension, role, sequence, enum, table, view, matview, function/procedure; a real dependency can push an entity later), in ONE transaction on PostgreSQL (`DBD_NO_TX` opts out). Pending migrations run first, **version by version**, each whole before the next — its creates and alters (dependency order), then the `.data.sql` scripts of the tables it alters or adds (one seeding a table the version adds runs after the create, and is listed), then its drops, then its record; then every entity re-applies its DDL (before 0.25 they ran entity by entity, so a jump failed where a stepwise upgrade did not). A version's `ALTER TYPE … ADD VALUE`s run at its head as `IF NOT EXISTS` and commit with everything before them (earlier versions recorded), so the rest of the version can use the values; if it then fails, the values stay and the DB records the version before. A migration script stating no `SET search_path` runs on the path its entity's CREATE runs on (the last `SET search_path` its DDL file states before the CREATE, else `source.search_path`, else the session default). On a jump, a table an earlier pending version adds is created from its current DDL, so a later version's `ADD COLUMN` to it fails (`already exists`). `apply -n <entity>` is refused while migrations are pending (naming them; its dry run too) — it used to record versions it never ran. Each DDL file stating no `SET search_path` is named before the run and in the preview (`apply` and `deploy`). After the plan commits: matview stamping (drift stamps in `dbd.matview_stamps`, never the matview's own COMMENT; a stamp a pre-0.25 dbd kept as the comment is copied there by the heal on upgrade, before the file's `COMMENT ON` can erase it), pg_cron sync, `apply.after`, then the configured grants (under `--scope` only on the schemas it builds); `apply.before` runs outside the transaction. On an unversioned database that is already built it says `vN recorded on a database that was already built but had no version`, not "Fresh install". **Refused before anything runs:** a `-e dev` run on a database marked prod (environment guard), and a project older than the database — `version guard: the database is at v3, but this project is at v2` (or `records no version`), no override; check out a newer revision. A pre-existing unstamped matview whose deployed query and index keys are the design's is stamped (brownfield diffs clean). `--with-policies` also applies RLS. `--dry-run` prints the order (no grants applied, no hooks run) after running apply's own gates — it refuses an unparseable file, a gap/closure conflict, an unknown `-n` or a missing hook file where apply would, names each hook the scope would skip — and honours the scope's `extensions:` allowlist; with a database configured (`-d`, `$DATABASE_URL`, a resolving `target.url`) it also checks the scope pin, the environment guard and the version guard, refuses a named apply over pending migrations and an unresolved `data.sql` TODO, and lists the pending migrations in the run's order (`⚠` on each destructive statement; a scoped run whose pending versions touch nothing in scope says the run records them); an unreachable configured DB fails the preview, a SQLite file that does not exist is not created (it reads as none); with none it stays offline
- `dbd import` — load staging data (CSV/TSV/JSON/JSONL; a `.json` file is a JSON array of records or JSON Lines — on Convex an array only; data files are read as UTF-8) from the `import/` convention; env-specific files under `import/<env>/<schema>/` — or directly in `import/dev/`/`import/prod/`, which are always env folders (SQLite's dev data lives there) — load only when `-e <env>` matches; a file in a deeper folder (`import/staging/sub/x.csv`) never loads and is named (`… not loaded — an import reads import/<schema>/<table>.<ext>, or import/<env>/<schema>/<table>.<ext> for env dev or prod, and no folder deeper`). A `-e dev` import into a database marked prod is refused (environment guard), and so is a database pinned to another scope (no `--allow-scope-change`; `-n -f` and the dry run, given a database, are checked for both). JSON keys name the columns — a key naming no column is refused, as a CSV header's is; a file setting a generated column is refused; ids (incl. `GENERATED ALWAYS`) load as given and each identity/serial sequence is moved past the largest id loaded (`setval` — the importing role needs `UPDATE` on it); `null` is SQL NULL for every type, the JSON value null in json/jsonb is written `{"$json": null}` (a one-key `$json` object is unwrapped one level, Postgres and SQLite); a column whose key no record carries takes its DEFAULT, a key only some records lack is NULL there on Postgres (SQLite: that record's DEFAULT). CSV/TSV are RFC 4180 on PostgreSQL and SQLite alike: the header names the target columns (matched as Postgres resolves names — exact, or folded to lower case), so column order is free; a header column the table lacks, or one named twice, is refused and that file loads nothing; quoted fields may hold delimiters, line breaks and doubled quotes; a quoted field is never NULL (`""` is the empty string); nothing is trimmed (a header `id, name` is refused); CRLF and a BOM are handled. On PostgreSQL CSV/TSV go through `COPY t (cols…) FROM STDIN WITH (FORMAT csv)`; JSON records are staged in the project's own `dbd."import_tmp:<project>"` and moved by `dbd.import_jsonb_to_table`, installed by the load in dbd's own `dbd` schema (no `staging` schema is created; an older database keeps a `staging.import_jsonb_to_table` — drop it if unused). Truncate (the import's tables together, before any load: one `TRUNCATE` on PostgreSQL, so FK-linked staging tables import together, a referenced one loaded first, and a table outside the import holding a key to one fails the import, named, nothing emptied; `DELETE FROM` one at a time on SQLite, referencing table first — a SQLite import loads and empties in the order of the foreign keys the database reports, since its verbatim DDL gives none, and `--dry-run` lists that order when the database exists; Convex's `--replace` always replaces, so `truncate: false` has no effect there) → load → call each staging table's one loader → `import.after`. The loader, among the procedures that read the table: the one named `import_<table>`; else the only one reading no other staging table; else the only one no other table claimed (preferring one that writes a same-named table). A procedure loads at most one table and is called once per import, chosen over every data file (so `-n` calls the same loader); only procedures are loaders — a function is never run. Refused before anything is truncated: a `-n` selecting no data file (`no entity named 'X'` / `X has no data file under import/` / the file belongs to another env), a data file outside a non-empty `import.staging`, a data file whose target is a view, matview or sequence, a loader tie (naming the candidates — name one `import_<table>`), and under `--scope` a staging table the scope keeps whose loader procedure it leaves out (`import refused: scope 'S' leaves out the loader of these staging tables…`). `-n <table> -f <file>` loads one explicit file (format from `.jsonl`/`.json`/`.tsv`, else CSV) and nothing else — no truncate, procedures or `import.after`; `import.staging` still applies; under `--scope` a declared table must be one the scope builds, an undeclared one loads with a warning. Under `--scope` an entry needs every table its procedure writes and its declared staging table. Nothing is skipped silently (`--dry-run` included, which also names each `import.after` hook the scope skips; it reads the database only for the pin and environment guards): the summary always states the table count — tables, not files — (including `0`) and warns with the reason — no `import/` dir, files belonging to another `-e <env>`, a staging file that failed to parse, an entry cut by `--scope` (`X not imported — T is outside scope 'S'`), a function that reads a staging table no procedure loads (`X has no loader procedure — function F reads it but is not run`), or a procedure that reads one without being its loader (`P reads X but is not called — L is its loader`)
- `dbd export` — export table data (scope-aware) to the project's `export/<schema>/<name>.<fmt>` (`-s`, wherever you run from; SQLite `export/<name>.<fmt>`); `-f/--format` sets the format (`csv`/`tsv`/`jsonl`; any other is refused), `-o/--output <dir>` replaces `export/` with the same layout (`<dir>/<schema>/<name>.<fmt>` — `-o import` for a round trip; before 0.25 `-o` wrote flat and same-named tables overwrote each other) — except a schema folder of the project's `import/` tree (`import/<schema>`, `import/<env>/<schema>`), where each file is `<name>.<fmt>`, as that import loads it (`export -n core.accounts -o import/staging` → `import/staging/accounts.csv` → `staging.accounts`); two tables that would share a file there are refused, the refusal saying to export there, with `-n`, the one table whose rows that file should hold. Generated columns are left out. Refuses a database pinned to another scope (no `--allow-scope-change`). Empty `export:` ⇒ every table; a list ⇒ only those — tables, views or matviews (a view exports the rows its query returns: views that dereference FKs to the staging tables' natural keys move a long-lived system's data to a new database — `dbd export -d $OLD -o import/staging`, each view named after the staging table it feeds, then deploy the new one). An entry naming nothing exportable is warned about, and one the scope leaves out is named (`export: X is outside scope 'S' — not exported`); the run counts tables and views apart (`Exporting 2 table(s) and 1 view(s)...`); a `-n` that selects nothing is an error. CSV/TSV are written as Postgres's `COPY` writes them, SQLite included — NULL empty, `''` as `""`, quoted where needed — so an export loads back to the same values on either engine (SQLite writes the header even for an empty table, and a BLOB as `\x…` hex, as Postgres writes a `bytea` — it wrote NULL); JSONL writes every column's key, keeps a json column's exact text and a string scalar, `null` for SQL NULL and `{"$json": null}` for the JSON value null
- `dbd refresh` — run `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW [CONCURRENTLY]` now (honoring each matview's resolved `concurrently`); `-n <entity>` or `-n <schema>.*` targets a subset, omit for all. Refuses a database pinned to another scope (no `--allow-scope-change`). Scheduled refresh is otherwise managed in-database via pg_cron (jobs named `dbd-refresh:<project>:<schema>.<name>`, each project's its own, synced on `apply`/`deploy`; needs the `pg_cron` extension)
- `dbd deploy --source owner/repo/path` — fetch + apply + grants (scoped) + import + policies (`deploy` = bring the DB fully up from source, so RLS from `policies/` applies unconditionally, unlike `apply`'s opt-in `--with-policies`; grants are the same `apply` applies, right after the schema). `deploy` is the ONLY command that takes a GitHub source (`owner/repo[/path][@ref]` or a github.com URL); others refuse one — clone and pass the path. `GITHUB_TOKEN` (private repos) is sent as a bearer token to `api.github.com` only. Honours `-c`. GitHub sources cache under `~/.cache/dbd` — `--no-cache` re-downloads this source, `--clear-cache` wipes the whole cache first. Every phase reports its count including `0`, in the order the phases ran, and a zero import states why (see `dbd import`); what the import phase would refuse (`import.staging`, a loader tie, a loader the scope leaves out) is refused before anything is applied, as are the apply phase's guards (scope pin, `-e dev` on a prod DB, an older project); a failed policy file is a **warning**, not a failure — it is counted in the summary and the deploy still succeeds. `--dry-run` runs the real gates (refuses an unparseable file, a gap or closure conflict) and reports after scope filtering: the scope line, `deps: include` gaps as `+ auto-included:`, entities to apply, data files to import with the reason for each left out and each `import.after` hook the scope skips, policy files applied/skipped; given a database it also checks the scope pin, the environment guard and the version guard and lists the pending migrations. `dbd deploy` is a thin wrapper over the library's `Design::deploy`, so an embedder gets the identical pipeline
- `dbd reconcile` — pre-release (pre-v1) **declarative** apply: diff the live DB against the design and apply `CREATE`/`ALTER` in place, no snapshots/version bump; scoped to managed schemas. Writes in one pass in `apply`'s dependency order (a function before a table whose default or trigger calls it). **Not one transaction**: each step commits as it runs, so a failing step stops the run with the earlier steps applied — only that step (one table's `ALTER` script, one enum's recreation) rolls back (an enum value added by `ADD VALUE` is unusable until committed, so the run cannot be wrapped). `--allow-destructive` drops columns/constraints on managed tables and removes enum values (Postgres has no `ALTER TYPE … DROP VALUE`, so the type is recreated: the managed views over a table with a column of the enum — and views over those — dropped, defaults taken off, type renamed aside and recreated, columns moved across via `::text::`, defaults restored, indexes reading the column (partial, expression) dropped and rebuilt around the swap, old type dropped, the views re-applied later in the run; tables, functions and procedures are never dropped; the recreation is one statement batch, so its failure is total for that enum — a row holding the value names its column; the type keeps its `COMMENT ON TYPE`; a **live** materialized view reading the column, directly or through views, refuses the run before any write, `--dry-run` too, exit non-zero, naming the `DROP MATERIALIZED VIEW` to run by hand before re-running `--allow-destructive`, which re-creates the matviews the design declares — dbd never drops one); without the flag the refusal lists each drop by entity (`app.t: drops column c`) and nothing else; `--prune` drops orphaned tables (in a managed schema, gone from the design); orphaned enums are only warned. Materialized views: create-if-absent (drift stamp recorded in `dbd.matview_stamps`); a drifted definition is only **warned**, never auto-dropped (a matview recreate is `DROP … CASCADE`, losing data/dependents — drop it manually, then `apply`/reconcile recreates it). Disabled once `project.released` (it checks only that flag). Converges columns (collation and a `nextval('s')` default included), PK/unique, FKs (`MATCH FULL`, deferral), CHECKs, EXCLUDE constraints, indexes (a key's backing index matched by the constraint's name, so a declared index over a key's columns is real) and column comments; what an extension owns is never read as drift or an orphan. `public` is managed only when the design puts something there — a role or an extension with no `schema:` does not count (before 0.25 it did, and `--prune` dropped undeclared tables in `public`). Records version 0 for a design with no `project.version` — and records it even over a newer database's (the older-project guard covers apply/deploy only). Runs the design's `apply.before`/`apply.after` hooks (before: after every gate, before the first write; after: after the writes and pg_cron sync) and then its grants (`Applied grants.`), scoped as `apply` scopes them, so a reconciled database is the one an apply builds; the summary adds `, N hook script(s) run`. A `-e dev` run on a database marked prod is refused. `--dry-run` refuses a database pinned to another scope or a `-e dev` run on a prod one, refuses a missing hook file, names the hooks the scope skips, and lists the hooks and grants the run goes on to apply; with a SQLite file that does not exist it previews against an empty in-memory database, creating no file
- `dbd diff` — read-only: show the complete live-DB↔design difference (columns with their collation, PK/unique, FK with `MATCH FULL`/deferral, CHECK, EXCLUDE, indexes — a dropped one over a key's columns included — column comments, enums — the same model reconcile converges; what an extension owns left out; diff also shows what reconcile won't touch: orphans without `--prune`, orphan enums, matview drift) plus **materialized-view drift** (each matview reported `missing`/`drifted`/`unstamped`/`orphan` via the `dbd:hash` drift stamp in `dbd.matview_stamps`; counts toward `--exit-code`, in `--json` as `matview_drift`). Table, view and enum comments are not compared. `--json` for tooling, `--exit-code` (0 in sync / 2 drift / 1 error). Tables + enums (structural) + matview drift; always available (even after release); refuses on scope dependency gaps; on a database pinned to another scope it notes the pin first (stderr under `--json`)
- `dbd release` (alias `dbd baseline`) — cut v1: write a baseline snapshot at the current `project.version` and set `project.released: true`, locking in the snapshot/migration workflow (disables `reconcile`). Refuses if already released or the design has errors. A project that already has snapshots (`init --from-db`/`merge` write them without setting `released`) is released at the version its latest snapshot reached, with no second baseline — refused while the design has changes no snapshot records, or `project.version` disagrees with the latest snapshot. Edits `design.yaml` in place (comments and layout kept), as `dbd snapshot` does
- `dbd combine` — combine DDL into single SQL file (scope-aware); generated statements follow the project's dialect — for T-SQL a guarded `CREATE SCHEMA` and every entity's DDL closed with its own `GO` batch (a file already ending in `GO` keeps its own), none for MySQL/SQLite, PostgreSQL-only extensions and roles as a comment; PostgreSQL output keeps `public` on a file's own path as apply does — after each top-level `SET search_path` (parse tree, so never a function's `SET` clause, a body, a literal or a comment) whose path lacks it, a statement of its own adds it; no file text is edited — and puts `SET search_path TO <source.search_path>, public` ahead of a file that states none, as apply runs it, so `psql -f` behaves like apply; `-f` must resolve inside the project (a bare name against the project root); an unparseable file is left out without a word
- `dbd emit --dialect mysql|tsql|sqlite [-f out.sql] [--report r.json]` — translate a PostgreSQL project's schema into another engine's DDL: tables with keys, FKs and CHECKs (with their names — a primary key's on SQL Server/SQLite, MySQL's always `PRIMARY` ⚠), indexes, identity/serial (`AUTO_INCREMENT`/`IDENTITY(1,1)`/`INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT`), generated columns, defaults (`now()`, `current_date`, `gen_random_uuid()` translated; a literal loses its `::cast`; the rest reported) and comments where the target keeps them; views/matviews as `CREATE VIEW` (a matview becomes a plain view, reported, its indexes left out). On MySQL/SQL Server a view's query and a CHECK pass through untranslated (reported); on SQLite (3.39+) both are written again from the parse tree — `core.cities` → `"core_cities" AS "cities"`, `POSITION(a IN b)` → `instr(b, a)`, NULL order / `LIKE` escape / column names spelled out — or, when SQLite cannot run a construct with the same meaning, the view or CHECK (and views reading it) is left out and reported, so the script applies. T-SQL also gets `CREATE SCHEMA` and `CREATE SEQUENCE` (`nextval` → `NEXT VALUE FOR`) and ends every statement with `GO` (the sqlcmd/SSMS separator — split on it before sending through a driver); MySQL/SQLite report sequences. Functions/procedures/triggers — a trigger in a table's file too — skipped (reported, and noted in the script); extensions, roles, grants (per schema) and RLS policies (per file) reported as not emitted; an FK to an `external:`/out-of-scope table left out (reported); a key column on unbounded text bounded (reported); an unparseable file reported as missing. Generated expressions and index predicates pass through untranslated (reported). MySQL gets `LONGTEXT`/`LONGBLOB` for `text` (and unbounded `varchar`)/`bytea` (its `TEXT`/`BLOB` hold 64 KB), `DATETIME(6)` (a clock default `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(n)`) and `TIME(6)`, and `JSON` for `json` (reported: MySQL normalises the document) and `jsonb`; `json`/`jsonb` are `nvarchar(max)`/`TEXT` ⚠ elsewhere. A `time` column's clock default is the time of day (`(CURRENT_TIME(p))` / `CONVERT(time, SYSDATETIME())` / `CURRENT_TIME`); a lost `NULLS NOT DISTINCT` ⚠ on MySQL/SQLite; an FK's `DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED` is carried to SQLite, and EXCLUDE, `COLLATE`, `MATCH FULL` and (elsewhere) deferral ⚠. A type past the target's documented limits is switched or clamped and reported: `varchar(n)`/`char(n)` past 4,000 → `nvarchar(max)` on SQL Server; past 16,383 → `MEDIUMTEXT`/`LONGTEXT` on MySQL (`char(n)` past 255 → `VARCHAR(n)`); `numeric(p,s)` to MySQL's 65 digits/30 scale or SQL Server's 38 (a bare `numeric` → `DECIMAL(65,30)`/`decimal(38,10)`, reported; SQLite reports a `NUMERIC` it may round — past 15 significant digits with a fraction, or 18 whole); a row too wide moves its widest non-key columns out of the row (MySQL to text, SQL Server `nchar` → `nvarchar`). `char(n)`/`real`/`time` map to the target's own types; `timetz` → `TIME(6)`/`time` ⚠/`TEXT`, `interval` → `VARCHAR(255)`/`nvarchar(255)`/`TEXT` ⚠, `inet`/`cidr` → `VARCHAR(49)`/`nvarchar(49)`/`TEXT` ⚠. Enum columns become `VARCHAR(255)`/`nvarchar(255)`/`TEXT` (reported as an enum only for a declared enum; another unmapped type is reported as unmapped); MySQL/SQLite fold the schema into the name (`schema_table`). A name holding the target's quote character is escaped as the target escapes it (SQLite doubles `"`, MySQL a backtick, SQL Server `]`). `-f` and `--report` must resolve inside the project (a bare name against the project root). Still unreported: identity `START`/`INCREMENT`, a `timestamptz`'s zone (MySQL `DATETIME`, SQLite `TEXT`), index keys past MySQL's 3,072 bytes or SQL Server's 900 (not checked), SQL Server's UNIQUE admitting one NULL, a column-level `CONSTRAINT x REFERENCES` name (lost), a `CREATE VIEW v (a, b)` column list (lost on every target). MySQL/SQL Server output is written from documented syntax, not run against a server. Exit 0 with downgrades — assert on the report. Refuses non-PostgreSQL projects
- `dbd graph` — dependency graph as JSON (scope-aware); stdout is only the JSON — a file that does not parse is named on stderr and left out of nodes, layers and edges, and so is `-v`'s count, so `dbd graph -v | jq` parses; `-n` naming an `external:` entity is refused, as on inspect/apply
- `dbd diagram` — build the schema model and open the hosted interactive viewer (model gzip-encoded in the URL fragment, client-side only; /projects remembers opened designs in localStorage); `--print-url` prints the link, `--site`/`$DBD_DIAGRAM_URL` overrides the base, `--json -f` writes the raw SchemaModel JSON (drop the file onto /diagram) (`version: 3` — `tables` (columns incl. `identity`/`generated`, indexes with `where`, `checks`) and `refs` (every FK) for the ER view, `stubs` for the tables FKs land on that the model does not carry (`kind` `external`/`out_of_scope`/`unresolved`), `entities`/`deps` for views, routines, triggers, sequences and the call graph (`uses` = a column's enum or sequence), `schemas` = every schema the model draws something in, `note`/`noteMd` comments on every kind, `history` for the per-snapshot changelog (under `--scope`, the working set incl. the closure), `enums` with their values); a `deps: include` closure that needs what the scope excludes is refused; a file that does not parse is named (`⚠ <file> could not be parsed, so <entity> is left out: …`) and the rest is drawn
- `dbd dbml` — generate DBML documentation (scope-aware: `--scope` filters to the scope's working set). Carries CHECKs (`checks` block), expression indexes (backticked), table UNIQUEs (as unique indexes with their name and the note `unique constraint`, read back by `init --from-dbml` as the named constraint), SQL value keyword defaults (`current_date`, `current_user`) as expressions, multi-line notes triple-quoted, index notes (`where:`, `order:`, `nulls not distinct` lines), generated columns and ALWAYS identities (custom properties `generated always as:` / `generated as identity:`), an enum column's type schema-qualified as the table's `search_path` resolves it, in DBML's enum spelling (`"app"."mo\"od"` when it needs quotes), every name in DBML's quoting — whatever it holds: a quote, a backslash, a space, a `'`, non-ASCII text — read back as itself, a column comment's line breaks (DBML `\n`), a CHECK's name, an index's method (`type:`) and its `INCLUDE`/operator classes/storage parameters (`include:`/`opclass:`/`with:` note lines), a named PK (`pk` index entry with `name:`) and a named FK (`Ref "name":`) — PostgreSQL's default names left out — and a stub for every referenced table it does not define — typed like the FK column that references it (else from the design, else `varchar`), with an `indexes { … [unique] }` entry per referenced column set, so `dbml2sql` output applies. A file that does not parse is named (`⚠ … could not be parsed, so X is left out`) and the document is still written (exit 0). Needs @dbml/core ≥ 5.0 for `checks`, ≥ 9.1 for custom properties. Not written (no DBML syntax): an FK's deferral/`MATCH FULL`, EXCLUDE, collations. An expression default or CHECK holding a backtick gives a document `init --from-dbml` refuses (DBML has no escape for one); a line break inside a CHECK's or index predicate's string literal comes back as a space
- `dbd snapshot` — diff vs latest snapshot, generate migration SQL; smart multi-snapshot splits renames/type-changes/enum-removals into safe stages (with `*.data.sql` corrections, run after every schema change of their version; an enum value removal is 2 stages and keeps the type's `COMMENT ON TYPE`). A table removed from the design is written as `DROP TABLE … CASCADE` in `migrations/<NNN>/<schema>/<table>.sql`, and the next `apply` runs it (a hand-written `<table>.drop.sql` wins) — only where the table exists, counting only drops that ran (before 0.25 the generated drop never ran)
- `dbd migrate` — show migration status (read-only; `--status`): `Database version: none recorded` for an unversioned DB; `Database is up to date.` only when the versions match; a database pinned to a scope is noted. Pending migrations are run by `dbd apply`, not here
- `dbd policies` — apply RLS policies from `policies/<schema>/<table>.sql` (idempotent, fail-forward). Also run unconditionally by `dbd deploy` / `Design::deploy`, and opt-in on `dbd apply --with-policies`. Scope-filtered: a policy's target is read from its path, and one whose table is outside the working set is skipped and reported rather than run against a plane that lacks its schema (a file off that layout has no derivable target and always applies); `--dry-run` lists would-apply and would-skip under separate headings. Scope-guarded: refuses a database pinned to another scope, with no bypass flag (it never re-pins) — `--dry-run` too, whenever a database is configured
- **Lifecycle hooks** — `apply.before` / `apply.after` run on `apply`, `deploy` and `reconcile` (after is post-entity, before the configured grants and `policies/`); `import.after` runs with the import phase — `dbd import` and `dbd deploy` — and **never on `dbd apply`**, so post-DDL SQL parked there silently does nothing on `dbd apply` — move it to `apply.after`. Entries are a path or `{script, writes}`; declare `writes:` when tables appear as `format()`/`array[…]` data rather than SQL identifiers, since derivation returns empty there. Under `--scope` a hook is skipped only when it touches a table the design manages outside the scope; the skip is named before the run and in the `apply`/`deploy`/`reconcile` dry runs (`Design::hook_skips`), an `import.after` skip in `import`/`deploy --dry-run`; a missing hook file is an error there too; `reconcile --dry-run` lists the hooks it would run. A hook stating no `SET search_path` runs on `source.search_path` (else the session default), and its bare names are judged as Postgres resolves them: statement by statement, along the path in effect there (`public` after it), to the first schema where the design has that table or view. A hook with no derivable deps and no `writes:` always runs — scope filtering is a correctness aid, not a security boundary
- `dbd doctor` — audit/migrate config + layout: old-format design.yaml, stale files, and every non-canonical DDL folder the scanner reads → singular (`ddl/functions/`→`ddl/function/`, `sequences`, and `materialized_views`/`matviews`/`matview` → `materialized_view`; collision keeps newer, backs up older as `.bkp`). Also reports misfiled view/matview DDL (a `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW` under `ddl/view/` or the reverse) with a move hint, and `ddl/extension/`/`ddl/schema/` files with the design.yaml entry each becomes (`add { name: citext, schema: ext } to the target's extensions: list…`) — neither auto-fixed; it counts what it fixed as it counts what it found (`0 issues fixed, 3 left to fix by hand.`). Always exits 0
- `dbd reset` — drop the project's own objects entity-level (functions/materialized views/views/tables/sequences/enums, reverse order, matviews before the views/tables they read; `CASCADE` on a full reset — a scoped reset never cascades: it drops without it, all or nothing, and refuses naming what outside the scope depends on what it would drop; the policies and triggers on the tables and views it drops go first, with them, so one calling an in-scope function does not refuse it); keeps schemas + extensions by default. Prints what it dropped (`Reset dropped 1 view, 2 tables.`, or `Reset dropped nothing — …`), read from the database before and after. `--schemas`/`--extensions`/`--clean` opt into DROP SCHEMA/EXTENSION (under `--scope`, only the extensions the scope installs); `--target <postgres|supabase|sqlite>` (default: the design's target key, i.e. the first `target:` entry; a Convex design is refused, and so — before connecting — is a target that is not the kind of database the connection reaches) sets the protected-schema set (`supabase` also protects `public`; every role the design declares — `ddl/role/` and `target.roles` — is dropped on a full reset, only for `postgres`, unless another database on the server holds it: that role is kept and named, its grants here still revoked). On SQLite it drops tables and views in one transaction with `PRAGMA defer_foreign_keys = ON`; `--schemas`/`--extensions` change nothing there, and say so. A reset under the all-scope, or under the scope the database is pinned to (a bare reset of a database built under a `default:` scope), also deletes the database's bookkeeping row (env, version, scope pin) — the way to rebuild as dev a database a run without `-e` marked prod; a narrower scope keeps it. Guarded by the bookkeeping env check (`dbd.meta` on Postgres/Supabase, `_dbd_meta` on SQLite; the `dbd` schema itself is never dropped) — refused when marked prod or `versioned at vN` (called a released project's database only when `project.released` is set) — + the scope guard; `--scope` restricts to the scope's objects (a wrong-scope reset is refused unless `--allow-scope-change`/`--force`). `--dry-run` checks the same guards when a database is configured (`-d`, `DATABASE_URL`, or a `target.url` that resolves), `--force`/`--allow-scope-change` honoured alike; an unreachable configured DB fails to connect; with none configured it is an offline preview. Before dropping roles it revokes what apply granted them (`schemas:`/target `grants:` — USAGE, table privileges, and the `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` entry the resetting user set) on every surviving schema; a role holding anything else here fails the reset naming the role and what it holds (`… holds privileges or owns objects reset does not revoke (it revokes only the schema grants design.yaml declares): …`) — never `DROP OWNED BY`. It deletes the `dbd.matview_stamps` rows of the matviews it drops
- `dbd format [--check]` — DDL formatter; river-style SELECT/VIEW bodies on by default (`query_style: river`/`none`, `gutter`). Changes layout and keyword case only: statement boundaries from libpg_query (a `BEGIN ATOMIC` body is one statement), a keyword recased where PostgreSQL's grammar reads it as one (a column named `name`, `value` or `level` keeps its case; built-in type names are recased with the keywords), and a new layout used only if it parses to the same libpg_query tree with every string literal, `$$`/`$tag$` body, quoted name and comment byte-for-byte the same — else the statement is only recased, else left as written; a file PostgreSQL's scanner cannot read is left unchanged (before 0.25 `E'it\'s; tricky'` came out across three lines). Formatting twice changes nothing (`format` then `format --check` passes); a comment beside or above a statement stays there. A table is laid out whatever its literals and names (`U&'…'`/`$$` defaults, quoted names, a column CHECK, a named column constraint, `TEMP`/`WITH (…)`/`PARTITION BY`/`INHERITS`/`TABLESPACE`) — but only one sqlparser 0.62 can read: `UNLOGGED`, `LIKE`, `EXCLUDE`, `USING <method>`, `OF <type>`, `PARTITION OF`, identity options beyond one, a key's `INCLUDE`/`WITH`/`USING INDEX TABLESPACE`, `NO INHERIT`, `ON DELETE SET NULL (<cols>)`, column `STORAGE`/`COMPRESSION`, `int ARRAY`, `WITHOUT OIDS`, `UESCAPE`, and an enum with a label holding a `'` are recased, not laid out. `keyword_case` covers `GENERATED`/`ALWAYS`/`IDENTITY`/`STORED`/`MATCH`/`RESTRICT`/`ACTION`/`VALID`/`DATA` and every other keyword the grammar reads (`ATOMIC`, `COLLATE`, `BIT`, `PARTITION BY RANGE` …), index methods and built-in type names; a word on the formatter's own list (`data`, `type`, `key`, `comment` …) is recased even where it names a column. `format` and `inspect --fix` write a file back in its own encoding (UTF-16 with BOM stays UTF-16; a UTF-8 BOM is kept). `--check` exits 1 if any file would change (drop-in for pre-commit; `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml` ships `dbd-format` + `dbd-format-system`)
- `dbd install` — install dbd's Claude Code assets (the `dbd` skill + `dbd-pattern-verifier` agent, embedded in the binary) so an AI assistant knows the schema-as-code conventions. Global (`~/.claude`, or `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`) by default; `--project` writes `./.claude` (shared with the team only if committed); `--dry-run` previews. Reports each asset created/updated/unchanged and is idempotent

Reverse-engineering coverage (`init --from-db`/`merge`): schemas (under `schemas:`, no `ddl/schema/` files), extensions (in the target's `extensions:` with their `schema:`, no `ddl/extension/` files), enums (with their comments; written inside a `duplicate_object` guard, so the file runs twice), tables (columns with their collation, defaults, identity, PK/FK/unique/check and EXCLUDE constraints — every key written with its name, `CONSTRAINT "<name>" …`, Postgres's generated names too; an FK's `MATCH FULL`/`DEFERRABLE`/`INITIALLY DEFERRED` — indexes incl. gin/gist/brin/hash, partial and expression indexes, comments, serial/identity columns, and triggers in the table's file — `CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER`, a constraint trigger after `DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS`), views (with their `INSTEAD OF` triggers) and materialized views (with their own comment as `COMMENT ON VIEW`/`COMMENT ON MATERIALIZED VIEW`, a legacy dbd drift stamp left out; matview definition + indexes from `pg_matviews`, written to `ddl/materialized_view/`), functions & procedures (verbatim), roles (opt-in `--roles`), standalone sequences (`CREATE SEQUENCE IF NOT EXISTS`); a table an FK reaches outside the captured schemas is declared `external:`. The DDL is re-runnable (`IF NOT EXISTS`, `OR REPLACE`), so the project applies back to its own database — recording the version, changing nothing — and to a fresh one, with an empty `diff`; it is fully qualified, so `inspect`, `apply` and `deploy` note "no SET search_path" on every file. Supabase's platform schemas are left out only on a Supabase database (`auth` + `storage`); every schema and extension left out is named. Left out entirely: what an extension owns (tables, views, matviews, sequences, enums, functions, schemas — for `diff`/`reconcile` too). Named as a warning, not captured: a partitioned table (captured as one plain table holding every row, its partitions folded in), `NOT VALID`/`NOT ENFORCED`/`NO INHERIT`, a PK/UNIQUE's deferral, `UNLOGGED`, inheritance, a disabled trigger. Neither captured nor named: domains and composite types (a column typed by one fails on a fresh database), identity `START`/`INCREMENT`, storage parameters (`fillfactor`), column `STORAGE`, row-level security and policies, comments on constraints, indexes and functions; a default holding a backslash reads as drift in `diff` against the database it came from. A DBML source (`--from-dbml`) = schemas/enums/tables/FKs; from dbd's own DBML, CHECKs with their names, identity (ALWAYS vs BY DEFAULT), serial, generated columns, column UNIQUE, partial/expression indexes and key order, schema-qualified enum column types and multi-line column comments survive, a table UNIQUE comes back as its named constraint, enum comments are lost; a stub table (recognised by the note `dbd dbml` gives it) comes back as an `external:` entry, never a table to build, its schema not added to `schemas:` (a Ref adds no schema either); index methods, `INCLUDE`, operator classes, storage parameters and PK/FK names (other than PostgreSQL's defaults) survive; an FK's deferral/`MATCH FULL`, EXCLUDE and collations do not; every unnamed index comes back named `<table>_idx` (a second one on a table collides on apply). A hand-written document is read as @dbml/core reads it (aliases, inline `ref:`, multi-line notes, `Note {}` blocks, one-line tables @dbml/core accepts — anything after a column, an enum value or a header on its line is refused, naming it — a bare `pk`/`unique` after a type, a `pk` index, `Ref name:`, index `type:`); a type in DBML's enum spelling (`"app"."mo\"od"`), or a quoted name the document declares as an enum, is that enum, any other quoted type its own SQL text; every name reads back as itself, and the DDL written doubles a quote in every identifier; a one-to-one `Ref: a - b` keys `b` (an inline `[ref: - t.c]` its own column); a many-to-many `<>` Ref and a `TablePartial` are refused with why; notes are dedented as @dbml/core does, except a closing `'''` line is layout; a one-line note loses leading whitespace. A SQLite source (`--from-db sqlite://…`) = tables/views/user-indexes captured verbatim from `sqlite_master` (CHECK/affinity/AUTOINCREMENT/WITHOUT ROWID preserved; a table's and a view's triggers written into its file; no schemas/enums/functions/sequences/roles). The reverse dialect (postgres vs sqlite target) is taken from the connection URL scheme.

Global flags: `-e dev|prod` (`development`/`production` accepted as aliases; anything else is an error; default `prod`) selects `import/<env>/` folders and is recorded in bookkeeping; a `-e dev` run (`apply`/`deploy`/`reconcile`/`import`, `import -n -f` and their dry runs) against a database marked prod is refused before any write — the mark moves only dev → prod (a promoting run says so), with no override, so build a dev database with `-e dev` from its first run (one built without it is marked prod: rebuild with `dbd reset --force` under the all-scope or its pinned scope, then `-e dev`). `--scope <name>` selects a `scopes:` entity subset; `--deps report|include` overrides that scope's gap policy for one run. **Gap-gated** (filter, and refuse on a gap under `report`): `inspect`/`apply`/`import`/`deploy`/`reconcile`/`diff`. **Filter-only**: `dbml`/`combine`/`emit`/`graph`/`diagram`/`export`/`reset`/`refresh`/`policies` (`inspect --scope` is where gaps surface). **Ignored with a warning** (`--scope` or `--deps`): `snapshot`/`release`/`migrate`/`doctor`/`init`/`merge`/`format`/`install`. `snapshot`/`release`/`migrate` ignore it deliberately: a snapshot records the *design*, not one database, so a scoped baseline would omit entities and make every later snapshot emit spurious `CREATE`s. Scope decides which migration steps *run*, not which exist — a removed table's drop runs under a scope occupying its schema, where the table still exists. All filter to the entity working set (`reset` drops those entities; `--schemas` additionally restricts the dropped schemas to the scope's).

## Architecture

- Parser: libpg_query (PostgreSQL's own grammar, via the `pg_query` crate) — every DDL entity type. sqlparser-rs remains for `dbd format` and enum-candidate detection, not for reading DDL.
- Adapters (all working):
    - PostgreSQL + Supabase (sqlx, `postgres://`) — COPY streaming import, namespace-aware catalog, one transaction per apply (committed early only at a version adding enum values); a server that does not answer fails within 5 s, naming `host:port`, never the URL
    - SQLite (sqlx-sqlite, `sqlite://`/`sqlite::memory:`/`file:`) — batched multi-row INSERT (≤500 rows or 32k binds per batch), trigger-aware DDL splitter, ~150 builtins + `sqlite_*` prefix recognised offline
    - Convex (codegen, `convex:`/`convex://<dir>[?deploy=true]`) — flattens names, maps SQL → `v.*` validators, enums emit `export const X = v.union(v.literal(…))` above `defineSchema`, single-column FKs emit `v.id("table")`; opt-in `npx convex deploy` after apply; `import_data` shells out to `npx convex import --replace` per table (so `truncate: false` has no effect); write the URL quoted in YAML (`url: "convex:"`)
- No MySQL or SQL Server adapter: `mysql://`/`mariadb://`/`sqlserver://`/`mssql://` URLs are refused by name. Their DDL is *read* (`tsql`/`mysql` readers: identity + references, no columns) and *written* by `dbd emit`
- Readers (`source.dialect`/`source.parser`): `pg_query` (structured — needed by diff/reconcile/emit), `tsql`, `mysql`, `verbatim` (SQLite). Every DDL reader — scan, apply, deploy, combine, format, doctor, merge, migrations — decodes UTF-8 or UTF-16 with a BOM
- Classification: adapter-owned — each adapter knows its target's catalog (Postgres queries pg_proc/pg_type, SQLite uses a sorted builtins list + `sqlite_*` prefix rule, Convex defers everything to user-defined)
- Parallel parsing: rayon for CPU-bound file parse, tokio for async DB operations
- Library-first: `dbd-core` crate for embedding, `dbd-cli` for the binary
- Reference cache: `inspect --from-db` snapshots all user-defined entities to `.dbd/refcache.json`; subsequent offline runs consult it to silence "Unresolved reference" warnings without a live DB

## Key types

- `Entity` — central type for all DDL objects
- `TableDef` — parsed table structure (columns, FKs with actions, indexes, constraints, comments)
- `EntityType` — Schema, Extension, Role, Sequence, Enum, Table, View, MaterializedView, Function, Procedure, Trigger (reported by the T-SQL/MySQL readers; dbd never applies one), External, Import
- `DatabaseAdapter` trait — connect, apply (single + batch, incl. transactional begin/commit/rollback batch), `execute_project_script` (a migration or hook on its search path), import/export (`truncate_tables` empties an import's tables together; `truncate_table` one), classify_reference, resolve_entity, list_entities, introspect (reverse-engineer) + `dependencies`, migration + meta tracking (`other_projects_meta` for a renamed project), `stamp_matview` / `forget_matview_stamps` (matview drift stamps), `matviews_reading_columns`
- `DatabaseMarks` — what a database records of the projects run against it, as every guard reads it (`Design::database_marks`); `Design::check_scope_guard` takes it (was `Option<&ProjectMeta>` in 0.24.1 — breaking)
- `RefCache` — JSON snapshot of remote entity names for offline `inspect`

## Safety

- The bookkeeping table records environment (dev/prod) and version in the database: `dbd.meta` in a dedicated `dbd` schema on Postgres/Supabase (paired with `dbd.migrations` and `dbd.matview_stamps`; not PostgREST-exposed, excluded from reverse-engineering/reset), `_dbd_meta`/`_dbd_migrations` on SQLite (no schemas there, so the prefix is the namespace). Legacy `public._dbd_meta`/`public._dbd_migrations` (and scoped-apply strays) heal into `dbd.meta`/`dbd.migrations` automatically on the next write — the project's own rows; another project's stay, with the legacy table, until that project heals
- `dbd reset` blocked when the database is marked prod (rows older versions wrote as `production` included — and any database applied without `-e dev` is prod), and at version ≥ 1 in any env (`versioned at vN`); `--force` overrides. `reset --dry-run` refuses the same way whenever a database is configured. A reset under the all-scope or the database's pinned scope deletes the bookkeeping row
- A `-e dev` run against a database marked prod is refused (`apply`, `deploy`, `reconcile`, `import`, `import -n -f`, and their dry runs) — it would lift reset's prod guard and load `import/dev/` data into production; dev may be promoted to prod (the run says so), never the reverse, and there is no override
- The record is keyed on `project.name`: when this project has none but the database holds its tables, views, matviews, enums or sequences, every guard reads the other projects' records (a renamed project), and a refusal names them — before 0.25 a rename lifted every guard. A renamed design whose run trips no guard is recorded beside the old record, and one ahead of the old record's version is planned as a fresh install (its migrations do not run): set `project.name` back first
- A dry run never creates a database: a SQLite file that does not exist reads as none configured, and `reconcile --dry-run` previews against an empty in-memory one
- A project older than the database (design v2, database v3; or an unversioned design) is refused by `apply`, `deploy` and their dry runs — no override
- `project.released` (set by `dbd release`) disables the in-place `dbd reconcile` workflow — after release, schema changes must go through snapshots + `dbd apply`
- `dbd reconcile` never touches schemas the design doesn't declare (`public` only when the design puts something there); column drops need `--allow-destructive`, whole-table (orphan) drops need `--prune`; under `--scope`, tables the design declares outside the scope are left alone, never pruned
- `--force` overrides safety guards
- For Convex (codegen target) the equivalent state lives in `<output>/.dbd_state.json`

## Skill & agent (for AI assistants)

dbd ships a Claude-Code **skill** (`dbd`, the schema-as-code mental model + workflow rules) and a **`dbd-pattern-verifier` agent** (reviews a project for convention conformance — right workflow for the release state, idempotent DDL, secrets, folder layout, enum-vs-CHECK, matview drift). Discover + install them via the `sensei.library.json` manifest, served at `https://dbd.sensei-hq.com/.well-known/sensei.library.json` (and in-repo at the root); raw files at `/skills/dbd/SKILL.md` and `/agents/dbd-pattern-verifier.md`.
